children: BlueScope Steel upgraded its guidance for first-half underlying earnings before interest and taxes, citing stronger-than-anticipated U.S. steel spreads.

The Australia-based steelmaker said Monday that it now expects underlying EBIT to approach 1.1 billion Australian dollars, equivalent to US$774 million, for the six months to Dec. 31. That is above its previous guidance of between A$860 million and A$960 million.
"Conditions across the U.S. steel industry and in our key North American end-use markets remain favorable," said Chief Executive Tania Archibald.

BlueScope now expects first-half benchmark U.S. spreads of roughly US$810 a metric ton, up from about US$750 a ton previously. Spreads represent the difference between the price of steel products and the raw materials needed to make them.

In addition to wider spreads, BlueScope's U.S. steel plant, North Star, is benefiting from a debottlenecking project that is expected to result in higher-than-anticipated volumes, the company said. North Star is now expected to deliver a first-half earnings result nearly three-quarters higher than in the second half of fiscal 2026.
The performance of BlueScope's North American buildings and coated-products business and its Australian steel products business has also improved, said Archibald.

BlueScope has been working on a turnaround of its coated-products business, the second-largest metal painter in the U.S., amid a wider campaign to improve efficiency and bolster investor returns. The steelmaker, the largest in Australia and fifth-biggest in the U.S., was recently the target of a takeover campaign involving Indiana-based Steel Dynamics.

"While market conditions remain dynamic, the performance we've seen through the first half reinforces our confidence in the strength of BlueScope's portfolio, the quality of our assets and our continued ability to deliver strong shareholder returns," Archibald said.
